scale_note: Working scale follows the source-photo pixel ratio and a plausible 600 ml aerosol-can size. It is not a measured dimension of the physical item.

proportion_source.reference_note: The six-view sheet is an uncalibrated visual match for the same Raid-type 600 ml aerosol can. Its panels are not a calibrated turntable: the top view is oval, the cap shape is simplified and the side-panel label ends do not join seamlessly. Front/back/side panels are used for the hidden-half label wrap and the top/bottom topology; the original photo decides proportions and the visible front design.
proportion_source.visible_structure: Cylindrical printed tinplate aerosol can with a rolled bottom rim and concave brushed-metal base; black glossy plastic overcap with two raised side horns, a saddle top and a two-lobed front/top window exposing the spray actuator; two small nozzle orifices; purple-to-pink Raid label with a white back information panel, barcode and insect icons.
proportion_source.pixel_ratios: Source silhouette is about 374 px wide and 1467 px tall (diameter/height about 0.255); the label body is about 374 px wide and 1138 px tall. The candidate uses 0.0664 m diameter and 0.262 m overall height, not measured dimensions.

dimensions.note: Dimensions are derived from the source-photo silhouette; the hidden can interior, wall thickness, valve cup and exact cap fit are inferred.

window.note: The two-lobed front window is inferred from the original photo and is a real hole through the solidified plastic shell. The cap is built as a surface with the window faces removed, then solidified, so the opening has a real wall rim; the exact outline and internal linkage are not measured. The uncalibrated top reference simplifies the cap and is not used as the window outline.

nozzle.note: Two real through-bores in the actuator face; the internal valve and trigger linkage are simplified and inferred.

checks_note: All checks are diagnostics. The six-view reference is uncalibrated; a candidate result is manual_only and cannot enter automatic placement or final compositing.
